# Final-round scheduling — Senior Backend Engineer (week of Mon 26 Oct 2026)

## 1. Schedules

**UTC offsets that week.** EU clocks go back on the last Sunday of October — **Sun 25 Oct 2026** — so from Monday Berlin is CET (**UTC+1**) and Lisbon is WET (**UTC+0**). US clocks don't go back until the first Sunday of November — **Sun 1 Nov 2026** — so New York is still EDT (**UTC−4**) and Chicago still CDT (**UTC−5**). This is the one-week mismatch: Berlin–New York is 5 h (normally 6), Lisbon–New York 4 h (normally 5), Chicago–Berlin 6 h (normally 7). All invites go out with explicit time zones.

Working hours in UTC: Jane 08:00–16:00 · Mary/John 13:00–21:00 (John free from 13:30) · Roe 09:00–17:00 · Miles 14:00–22:00.

No interviewer conflicts on Wednesday; everyone within hours; each interviewer does one session per day.

## 2. Why these days and slots

**Day allocation.** Both candidates offered Tuesday, but the one-session-per-interviewer-per-day rule means they can't share it. Miles's only alternative is Thursday, when Jane is out of office — so Miles **must** be Tuesday, which pushes Roe to Wednesday (his other day, and conflict-free). Monday and Friday weren't offered by either candidate.

**Tuesday (Miles).** Jane is the binding constraint: busy until 15:00 CET (14:00 UTC) and finished by 17:00 CET (16:00 UTC), while Miles's day only starts at 14:00 UTC. So Jane's slot has to sit in 14:00–16:00 UTC, and I put her first because that window is the scarcest. With the 30-minute breaks Miles requested, a Jane-first loop means the second session starts 15:30 UTC — inside Mary's 15:00–16:00 UTC conflict — so John goes second and Mary third.
Ruled out: Mary-first (Mary 14:00, Jane 15:15–16:00, John 16:30 UTC) — valid, but it ends Jane exactly at 17:00 CET and starts Miles at 09:00 sharp; too tight. Jane at 14:00 UTC — back-to-back with her two-hour meeting. Thursday — Jane OOO.

**Wednesday (Roe).** The loop has to fit between New York's 13:00 UTC start and Roe's 17:00 UTC finish, with Jane done by 16:00 UTC and John free from 13:30 UTC. Starting at 13:30 UTC gives Mary 09:30 rather than 09:00 sharp, keeps Jane comfortably inside her day, and gives John the same 11:30 EDT slot both days. Standard 15-minute breaks keep Roe's loop compact (13:30–16:15). Tuesday was feasible for Roe in isolation (e.g., Mary 13:00, Jane 14:00, John 15:00 UTC) but blocked by the one-per-day rule.
